standard.title: Business adaptation
standard.description: different ways that businesses adapt to opportunities in the market and respond to the changing nature of work
standard.prior_knowledge: Students understand the reasons businesses exist and how different types of businesses provide goods and services (AC9HE7K02). They understand entrepreneur characteristics and how these influence business success (AC9HE7K03). They understand how markets allocate resources through price signals (AC9HE8K01).
standard.progression_endpoint: Students discuss different ways that businesses adapt to opportunities in the market and respond to the changing nature of work.

nodes.label: Identifying market opportunities
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how businesses identify needs, niches and gaps in established markets and how these guide the development of new products or services.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify one example of a business that identified a gap or niche in the market and explain how that opportunity guided what it produced or offered.
nodes.typical_width: Explain how businesses systematically identify needs, niches and gaps in established markets, and how this analysis shapes the development of specific goods or services. Use two or more examples drawn from different market sectors (e.g. electric vehicles, solar energy, health tech).
wider: Investigate how market research methods (surveys, data analytics, focus groups) help businesses identify opportunities before a product or service exists

Examine how disruptive innovations create entirely new market categories rather than filling existing gaps — e.g. how streaming services did not just fill a gap in DVD rental but eliminated the category
Research how social enterprises and not-for-profit businesses identify opportunities that traditional profit-seeking businesses overlook, particularly in underserved communities
nodes.hinge_reason: Understanding how businesses identify opportunities is the foundation for explaining both technology-driven adaptation and workforce change — students who cannot explain this link will treat later nodes as disconnected examples rather than a coherent picture of business adaptation.

response_modes.reason: Students need a range of concrete business examples — across industries and scales — to see that opportunity identification is a generalised business behaviour, not a quirk of specific companies. Build the repertoire before asking for analysis.

success_criteria: Identifies a market need, niche or gap that a real business responded to
Explains how identifying that opportunity influenced what the business decided to produce or offer

nodes.label: Technology-driven business adaptation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how businesses use technologies to streamline operations or gain efficiencies, using specific examples such as ride share, food delivery and online retail.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe how one business has used a specific technology to streamline its operations or improve efficiency, naming the technology and the efficiency gained.
nodes.typical_width: Explain how businesses across different sectors use technologies to streamline or gain efficiencies in existing business models, including platform-based models (ride share, food delivery apps) and online retail. Discuss both the business benefit and the market opportunity created.
wider: Investigate how automation and artificial intelligence are being adopted by Australian businesses (e.g. retail checkout, logistics, accounting) and the efficiency gains and workforce implications
Examine how data analytics and algorithmic tools allow businesses to personalise offerings at scale — e.g. streaming recommendations, targeted advertising, dynamic pricing

Compare how a traditional business model in one sector (e.g. taxi industry, physical retail) was disrupted by a technology-enabled competitor, analysing what the incumbent was slow to adapt to and why

response_modes.reason: Students often confine technology adaptation to the most prominent examples (Uber, Amazon). Wider sector examples reveal that technology-driven efficiency is a cross-industry pattern, not a Silicon Valley phenomenon.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Technology adoption examples span every sector students will encounter professionally or as consumers. Wider contexts — automation in manufacturing, AI in services, data analytics in retail — give students a richer and more transferable picture of how businesses adapt through technology.
success_criteria: Names a specific technology a business adopted and describes the efficiency or market opportunity it created
Explains the connection between the technology adoption and the business's ability to serve customers or compete in the market

nodes.label: Changing nature of work
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain current and historical influences on how people work, including technological change, globalisation, communication changes and workforce casualisation.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify and explain two influences on the changing nature of work in Australia (e.g. technological change and casualisation), giving at least one concrete example for each.
nodes.typical_width: Explain multiple influences on the ways people work including: technological change, outsourced labour in the global economy, rapid communication changes, and casualisation of the workforce. Use specific Australian examples and explain how each influence changes employment arrangements or job types.
wider: Investigate changes to the Australian workforce over time using data: jobs growth and decline across industries, changing career length patterns, and shifting demographic composition of the workforce

Examine the gig economy in Australia — the rights and responsibilities of workers in platform-mediated casual work (ride share, food delivery, freelance platforms) and the policy debates around classification as employees vs. contractors
Research how corporate social responsibility, sustainability practices and changing consumer values are influencing what kinds of work businesses create and how they manage human resources

response_modes.reason: The descriptor lists four distinct influences. Students need grounded examples of each before they can discuss the descriptor's full scope. Build the repertoire of influence-type → example pairs before synthesis.

success_criteria: Names at least two distinct influences on the changing nature of work
Explains, using a specific example, how one of these influences has changed the way a type of work is performed or organised in Australia

nodes.label: Business adaptation — integrated
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can discuss how businesses adapt to market opportunities and the changing nature of work, connecting opportunity identification, technology use, and workforce change into a coherent account of business adaptation.
nodes.minimum_width: Discuss how one business has responded to both a market opportunity and the changing nature of work, explaining how these two dimensions of adaptation are connected.
nodes.typical_width: Discuss how businesses adapt to market opportunities and respond to changes in the nature of work, drawing on the full range of adaptation types: identifying gaps, deploying technology, and restructuring how work is organised. Use at least two detailed examples.
wider: Evaluate how a business's adaptation strategy has created benefits for some stakeholders (shareholders, consumers) while creating costs or disruptions for others (workers displaced by automation, local suppliers replaced by global outsourcing)
Investigate how a First Nations Australian business has adapted to market opportunities in ways that integrate cultural values and responsibilities to Country alongside commercial goals
Research a business that failed to adapt — analyse what opportunities or changes it missed and what the consequences were for the business, its workers, and its market

response_modes.reason: Students should demonstrate that market opportunity identification, technology adoption, and workforce change are not three separate topics but interconnected dimensions of how businesses respond to their environment. The integration task should require connecting at least two of these.

success_criteria: Discusses at least two ways a business adapts to opportunities or changing work conditions
Connects the business's adaptation choices to a specific market opportunity or work-related change, using appropriate terminology
